# Changelog

Hand-written notes for each release, newest first. The release workflow copies
the section for the version being released into the GitHub release as
"Highlights"; the list of merged pull requests below it is generated by GitHub.

## 1.6.0

### Behavior changes

Complexity scores change for some code, so a threshold gate that passed with
1.5.0 can fail after upgrading. Raise the threshold or add a
`// swift-complexity:disable` comment above declarations whose complexity is
accepted.

- Cyclomatic complexity now counts the ternary operator (`a ? b : c`),
  nil-coalescing (`??`), each additional comma-separated condition in `if`,
  `else if`, `guard` and `while` (`if let a, b` adds 2), and the `where`
  clause of a `for` loop. The syntax tree is operator-folded before analysis;
  previously `?:` and `??` were never counted. (#59)
- Cognitive complexity now counts the ternary operator. `??` stays uncounted,
  following the SonarSource definition. (#59)
- Nested functions, local types and local computed properties are no longer
  counted twice: each is reported on its own and no longer adds to the
  enclosing function. (#59)
- `#if` / `#elseif` / `#else` contribute only their most complex clause
  instead of the sum of all clauses. (#59)

### Bug fixes

- `--cyclomatic-only` and `--cognitive-only` now gate on the selected metric
  only: the threshold filter, exit code, Xcode diagnostics, SARIF results,
  hotspot ranking and the MCP `cyclomatic_only` / `cognitive_only` parameters
  ignore the other metric. Previously the flags only changed the displayed
  column, so `--cognitive-only --threshold 9` failed on a function with
  cyclomatic 9 and cognitive 1. (#53, #61)

### Documentation

- `docs/user-guide/complexity-metrics.md` now matches the implementation:
  `switch` itself and `default` do not add to cyclomatic complexity (only
  `case` labels do), and closures count toward the enclosing function. (#59)
